questions.question: Compare 98 765 and 102 345. Which number is greater, and why?
options: 102 345, because it has six digits and 98 765 has only five
98 765, because if you start comparing at the ones place, 5 equals 5 and then 6 is greater than 4
98 765, because 9 is greater than 1
98 765, because its largest digit, 9, is bigger than every digit in 102 345
questions.explain: Count the places first: a six-digit number reaches the hundred thousands, so 102 345 is greater than any five-digit number like 98 765. The trap is comparing the 9 with the 1 — those digits sit in different places, so 9 ten thousands is being compared with 1 hundred thousand.

questions.question: Put these three numbers in order from least to greatest: 89 999, 100 001, 98 000.
questions.explain: Sort by how many digits first — 100 001 is the only six-digit number, so it is the greatest; then compare 89 999 and 98 000 in the ten thousands place, where 8 is less than 9. The trap is putting 100 001 first because it begins with a small digit 1.

questions.question: Which statement about 316 480 and 316 840 is true?
options: 316 480 is greater than 316 840, because 8 tens is greater than 4 tens
The two numbers are equal, because they are built from the same six digits
316 480 is less than 316 840, because 4 hundreds is less than 8 hundreds
The two numbers are equal, because both of them have six digits
questions.explain: Line the numbers up and compare from the left: the hundred thousands, ten thousands and thousands all match, so the hundreds place decides, and 4 hundreds is less than 8 hundreds. Using the same digits in a different order does not make two numbers equal.

questions.question: Which of these four numbers is the greatest: 612 500, 621 500, 98 750, 620 999?
questions.explain: Drop 98 750 first because five digits can never beat six, then compare from the left: the ten thousands place rules out 612 500, and in the thousands place 621 500 has 1 thousand while 620 999 has 0 thousands. A long string of 9s does not make a number bigger.

questions.question: In one month, four ferry routes carried these numbers of passengers: Route A 148 060, Route B 99 500, Route C 148 600, Route D 84 999. Which route carried the most passengers?
options: Route C, with 148 600
Route A, with 148 060
Route B, with 99 500
Route D, with 84 999
questions.explain: Rule out the five-digit totals first, then compare 148 060 and 148 600 from the left — they match down to the hundreds place, where 6 hundreds beats 0 hundreds. The trap is stopping at the 9 in 99 500 because it looks like a big digit.

questions.question: Four ski hills recorded these skier visits last season: Hill W 987 400, Hill X 405 200, Hill Y 98 700, Hill Z 45 200. Order the hills from greatest to least visits.
options: Hill W 987 400; Hill Y 98 700; Hill X 405 200; Hill Z 45 200
Hill W 987 400; Hill X 405 200; Hill Y 98 700; Hill Z 45 200
Hill X 405 200; Hill W 987 400; Hill Y 98 700; Hill Z 45 200
Hill Z 45 200; Hill Y 98 700; Hill X 405 200; Hill W 987 400
questions.explain: Split by digit count first — the six-digit totals 987 400 and 405 200 both beat the five-digit totals — then compare inside each group from the left. The trap is putting 98 700 right beside 987 400 just because both begin with 9.

questions.question: A digit is missing from a number: 4 _ 8 250. Which digit can go in the blank to make 4 _ 8 250 greater than 458 250?
options: 0, because 408 250 still starts with a 4
5, because 458 250 matches 458 250
6, because 468 250 is greater than 458 250
Any digit works, because both numbers have six digits
questions.explain: The hundred thousands digits are both 4, so the ten thousands place decides: you need a digit greater than 5, and 6 gives 468 250. Putting 5 in the blank makes the two numbers equal, not greater.

questions.question: Four community centres raised money for new playground equipment: Coquitlam $109 450, Langley $190 045, Mission $100 945, Sooke $94 500. Which centre raised the most money?
options: Coquitlam, $109 450
Mission, $100 945
Sooke, $94 500
Langley, $190 045
questions.explain: $94 500 has only five digits, so it is out right away; among the six-digit amounts the hundred thousands digits all match, so the ten thousands place decides — 9 for $190 045 against 0 for the others. Do not pick $94 500 just because it starts with a 9.

questions.question: Ravi says that 89 999 is greater than 105 000 'because 8 is greater than 1.' Which response correctly fixes Ravi's thinking?
options: Ravi compared digits from different places: 105 000 reaches the hundred thousands and 89 999 does not, so it is greater.
Ravi should compare starting at the ones place: 9 is greater than 0, and every 9 beats every 0, so 89 999 is greater.
Ravi is close enough: both numbers are about 100 000 when you round, so neither one is really greater than the other.
Ravi is right: 8 is greater than 1, and the first digit always decides which is bigger, so 89 999 is greater than 105 000.
questions.explain: Before comparing single digits, check how far each number reaches — 105 000 fills the hundred thousands place while 89 999 stops at the ten thousands, so 105 000 is greater. Matching the 8 against the 1 compares 8 ten thousands with 1 hundred thousand, which are not the same size.

questions.question: Three vehicles are in for service at a Kamloops garage: a car that has travelled 148 970 km, a truck that has travelled 148 790 km, and a motorcycle that has travelled 98 600 km. Order the vehicles from least distance travelled to greatest.
options: truck 148 790 km; car 148 970 km; motorcycle 98 600 km
motorcycle 98 600 km; truck 148 790 km; car 148 970 km
motorcycle 98 600 km; car 148 970 km; truck 148 790 km
car 148 970 km; truck 148 790 km; motorcycle 98 600 km
questions.explain: 98 600 has only five digits, so it is the least; then compare 148 790 with 148 970 from the left — they match to the thousands, and 7 hundreds is less than 9 hundreds. The trap is placing 98 600 last because it starts with 9.

questions.question: An arena holds 54 500 fans. Attendance was 47 950 on Friday, 54 050 on Saturday and 45 970 on Sunday. Which statement is true?
options: Sunday drew the biggest crowd, because 45 970 ends with the largest three digits.
Saturday drew the biggest crowd and the arena was full, because 54 050 and 54 500 both start with 5.
Saturday drew the biggest crowd, but the arena was not full, because 54 050 is less than 54 500.
Friday drew the biggest crowd, because 47 950 has a 9 in the hundreds place.
questions.explain: Order the three crowds from the left — only 54 050 has 5 ten thousands, so Saturday was busiest — then compare 54 050 with the capacity 54 500, where the hundreds place (0 against 5) shows the arena was not full. Two numbers starting with the same digit are not automatically equal.

questions.question: A BC charity set a goal of $500 000. Four regions reported these totals: $498 750, $512 500, $489 000 and $450 000. Which total is closest to the $500 000 goal?
questions.explain: Compare each total with $500 000 place by place, then estimate the gap: $498 750 is only $1 250 away, while $512 500 is $12 500 over and $489 000 is $11 000 short. The trap is choosing $512 500 because it also begins with a 5.
